chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, and a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn Uthman from Al-Qasim ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you enter from the door of Al-Baqie, the house of Ali (peace be upon him) is on your left, at the distance of a goat's passage from the door, and it is beside the house of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and their two doors are joined together.'

key_terms.الْبَقِيعِ: Al-Baqie, the main cemetery in Medina
key_terms.بَيْتُ عَلِيٍّ: The house of Ali, referring to his burial place
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: Where is the house of Imam Ali located in Al-Baqie cemetery according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi offers a precise topographical account of Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) resting place in Al-Baqie, emphasizing its proximity and structural connection to the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) house, which underscores their unique spiritual and familial bond. The description of their doors being 'connected' (maquran) is often interpreted by Shia scholars as a symbol of the inseparable link between the Imamate and the Prophethood, as well as the continuity of divine guidance. This geographical detail serves not only as historical record but also as a focal point for ziyarat (visitation) practices, reinforcing the physical sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt.
